about: Source registry for freebie-tracker. type=feed sources are pulled by tracker.py. type=page sources are official program/deal pages an agent checks on a slower rhythm. type=social sources are hunting grounds read by the agent leg (never scraped blindly). wake=true means new entries from this source may wake the agent; firehose sources are diffed and stored but never wake the agent alone.

sources.name: Baipiaoji limits.json
sources.notes: Machine-readable list of AI free quotas. Only lists entries traceable to official provider sources.

sources.name: Lanmao offers list
sources.notes: 341+ AI free-quota offers, claimed manually verified with dates and claim thresholds, updated daily. Many entries are China-shaped or real-name walled; the safety filter decides.

sources.name: Jidan credit list RSS
sources.notes: Curated free-credit postings.

sources.name: LINUX DO welfare section
sources.notes: The welfare (freebie) section of the LINUX DO community, read through the Jina reader. High signal for China-side giveaways, credits and trials.

sources.name: V2EX promotions feed
sources.notes: Promotions board of V2EX. Mixed quality; relays and resales fail the filter.

sources.name: LowEndTalk offers board
sources.notes: The Western hosting community's offers category. Provider giveaways surface here (a 100x free VPS for a year giveaway by RackNerd/AdminBolt was caught from this community). Feed carries the latest 100 offer threads.

sources.name: LowEndSpirit free offers feed
sources.notes: Sister community of LowEndTalk; this feed is restricted to the Free Offers and Stuff category, so it is the cleanest free-VPS signal outside the curated lists (free NAT VPS trials without a card, free hosting, community free VPS programs). Some offers are gated by forum participation (account age, post count) and a few threads are long-lived pinned offers; the feed itself is low volume, so it may wake.

sources.name: NodeSeek RSS
sources.notes: Hosting/VPS community firehose. Mostly marketplace chatter; read on wake by other sources, never a wake trigger by itself.

sources.name: Appinn feed
sources.notes: Chinese software deals and freebie blog.

sources.name: GuoHuangXi (ghxi.com) feed
sources.notes: Chinese software freebies and license giveaways.

sources.name: iPlaySoft feed
sources.notes: Chinese software discovery blog with frequent free offers.

sources.name: Slickdeals frontpage
sources.notes: US consumer deals community, frontpage feed. Mostly consumer offers; read on wake, never a wake trigger by itself.

sources.name: OzBargain feed
sources.notes: Australian deals community feed. Consumer offers with occasional software and hosting deals; read on wake, never a wake trigger by itself.

sources.name: Giveaway of the Day
sources.notes: Daily software giveaway site running since 2006; developers pay for promotion, so listings are real, but licenses usually must be installed and activated the same day and exclude upgrades and support. The site feed redirects to FeedBurner; the puller follows redirects.

sources.name: LowEndBox offers blog
sources.notes: Editorial sibling of the LowEndTalk forum: provider offers and giveaways curated by editors (a RackNerd bonus-code giveaway drop was visible at adoption). Mostly paid cheap deals rather than freebies, so it is firehose class: diffed and stored, read on wake, never a wake trigger by itself.

sources.name: AIHot free tokens page
sources.notes: Curated AI free-token page. No stable machine structure, so the agent reads it on wake; content largely overlaps lanmao and baipiaoji.

sources.name: free-for.dev list
sources.notes: The classic community list of free tiers for developers. Entries inherit a category from the section they sit in. Changes here usually mean a free tier appeared, changed, or died.

sources.name: free-ai-apis list (OuterSpacee)
sources.notes: Companion to free-for.dev for AI APIs: 100+ official free APIs in 15 categories with explicit free-tier and auth columns and a stated no-credit-card principle. Entries are keyed by provider domain, so several APIs on one domain collapse into a single entry; at adoption it parsed to 84 entries. Starts as firehose: its update rhythm is slower than free-for-dev, and the agent reads it on wake.

sources.name: GeekNews (news.hada.io)
sources.notes: Korean developer news aggregator. Korean government support programs, AI subsidy calls and startup credits surface here early.

sources.name: NIPA AI Voucher Programme (MSIT)
sources.notes: Korea's flagship AI subsidy: vouchers up to KRW 200M for SMEs and mid-sized firms to adopt AI solutions, government covers up to 80 percent. Annual call, typically announced Feb-Mar, applied through NIPA with a supplier consortium. Related tracks: AX One-Stop Voucher (AI + cloud + data), Data Voucher, K-Cloud project GPU support.

sources.name: K-Startup portal
sources.notes: Single registration portal for Korean government startup programs (Ministry of SMEs and Startups). Includes the K-Startup Grand Challenge, which is open to foreign teams.

sources.name: Bizinfo (government support aggregator)
sources.notes: Aggregates Korean government support program announcements across ministries. The page an agent checks when a Korean subsidy call is rumored.

sources.name: IndiaAI Mission
sources.notes: India's national AI mission. Its compute pillar gives subsidized GPU cloud through 14 government-empanelled providers (38,000+ GPUs; MeitY reports average subsidized tariffs around ₹65 per GPU hour). Stated open to startups, researchers, academia and government bodies via the IndiaAI Compute Portal (compute.indiaai.gov.in); official documents opened do not mention foreign entities, so treat as India-ecosystem only until verified otherwise. Watch: new provider empanelments, tariff updates, capacity expansions.

sources.name: J-Startup (METI)
sources.notes: METI's selective startup certification, not a cash grant: logo rights, promotion, minister-led overseas missions, exhibition support, preferential handling in support measures, large-company matching and regulatory-sandbox access, for roughly 200 firms picked from a pool of about 10,000. Historically nomination-only (designated VCs and accelerators propose candidates); round 6 in 2026 added an open application track (21 Oct to 13 Nov 2026, results Feb 2027). Foreign companies as defined by Japan's Companies Act are explicitly excluded. Watch: METI press releases opening each round.

sources.name: EuroHPC JU access calls
sources.notes: Free compute allocations on EU AI Factories supercomputers via the AI for Industrial Innovation modes: Playground (small, rolling, decided in about 2 working days), Fast Lane (up to 50,000 GPU hours) and Large Scale (over 50,000 GPU hours, allocations up to 1 year, two cut-offs per month). Apply at access.eurohpc-ju.europa.eu. Free eligibility requires establishment in an EU member state, a EuroHPC Participating State or a Horizon 2020 associated country (list includes the UK, Switzerland, Norway, Israel, Türkiye); entities outside that list cannot take the EU-funded share. Watch: call status, Large Scale cut-off dates, system availability notices.

sources.name: AI Singapore programmes
sources.notes: Singapore's national AI programme. 100 Experiments (100E): co-funding up to SGD 150,000 per project while AISG's own AI Engineering Hub team builds and deploys an AI MVP with the sponsoring organisation over about 6 months; sponsors match with cash and in-kind contributions, and a 3-month POC track also exists. AI Apprenticeship Programme (AIAP): full-time 6 or 9 month apprenticeships with a SGD 4,000/month stipend in roughly twice-yearly batches, restricted to Singapore citizens; PRs and foreigners are not eligible. Watch: AIAP batch openings and deadlines at aiap.sg, 100E track changes.

sources.name: AWS Activate
sources.notes: Startup cloud credits. Application-gated and card-gated: reference only for owners who can pass verification; the safety filter marks it gated.

sources.name: Google Cloud for Startups
sources.notes: Startup credits including AI-first tiers. Card verification required: gated reference only.

sources.name: Microsoft for Startups
sources.notes: Founders Hub credits for Azure and AI services. Application-based: gated reference only.

sources.name: GitHub Student Developer Pack
sources.notes: Large bundle of free tiers for verified students. New partner offers appear here first; worth an agent page check each cycle.

sources.name: X freebie hunter accounts
sources.notes: Accounts that habitually post free tiers, credits and giveaways. zhanx888 is a gray source (some content is bait): apply the strictest filter. X cannot be pulled by machine without the paid API or a logged-in session; the agent reads these on wake, with the owner's permission.

sources.name: Vietnamese VPS community groups (Facebook)
sources.notes: Provider giveaways surface here first (a first-come-first-served VPS giveaway by InterData was found in diendanservervpscloudvn). Public code drops are usually gone within hours, so latency matters.
